articles.title: Lanterns Episode 3 Teaser Reveals First Look at Hal Jordan Wearing Iconic Green Lantern Domino Mask
articles.summary: HBO has published the first teaser for Lanterns Episode 3, and it comes with a first look at Hal Jordan wearing Green Lantern's iconic domino mask.
articles.body:
HBO has published the first teaser for Lanterns Episode 3, and it comes with a first look at Hal Jordan wearing Green Lantern's iconic domino mask.

The network dropped the latest trailer for its DCU show following the conclusion of Episode 2 last night. If you didn't catch it after the credits rolled, the full 42-second Lanterns teaser can now be found on the HBO Max YouTube channel .

Don't worry; it doesn't give away too much. As has already been teased, John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) is being set up to be a special part of the DCU as episodes roll out. That means confronting what seems to be a Guardian (played by Laura Linney) and reckoning with his past. If the Lanterns Episode 3 teaser is anything to go by, the Green Lantern-in-training seems to be the star of next week's episode, but the moment that has everyone talking online actually concerns a blink-and-you'll-miss-it moment featuring Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler).

John Stewart was born for this. Watch new episodes of #Lanterns on Sundays at 9pm on HBO Max. pic.twitter.com/9SMnO7rINT — HBO Max (@hbomax) August 24, 2026

John Stewart was born for this. Watch new episodes of #Lanterns on Sundays at 9pm on HBO Max. pic.twitter.com/9SMnO7rINT

Just after the 17-second mark, you can see a few frames from an old TV playing what seems to be footage of the news covering Hal Jordan. He appears to be suited up in the same outfit we've seen Chandler wear in the show itself, but the main difference here is his bright-green domino mask.

So far, Chandler has given DC fans a slightly grumpier version of the Green Lantern they might be used to. While he's generally been hailed as a fitting inclusion for the DCU, connecting his character to the one we've seen featured in comic books and animated projects for decades has been a bit difficult for some. Seeing him suited up in full Green Lantern Corps attire seems to have already helped connect those dots for those fans online.

Warning! Spoilers for Lanterns Season 1 Episodes 1 and 2 follow.

All of that said, this may be a little more than an Easter Egg rather than a sneak peek at what this particular costume will eventually look like in motion. For starters, the end of Episode 1 pretty heavily implied that Hal Jordan's days in the DCU are already numbered . The Episode 3 teaser also suggested that we'll be skipping around the timeline yet again, potentially traveling back to 1996. If we do see Hal Jordan sporting his domino mask, those moments may be limited to a few flashback sequences.

New look at Hal Jordan wearing a domino mask in 'LANTERNS'. pic.twitter.com/d20PWHm6II — DC Film News (@DCFilmNews) August 24, 2026

New look at Hal Jordan wearing a domino mask in 'LANTERNS'. pic.twitter.com/d20PWHm6II

MASKED HAL JORDAN YOOOOO #Lanterns pic.twitter.com/R61q87Psp2 — Axel🦇 (@AxelTalksFilm) August 24, 2026

MASKED HAL JORDAN YOOOOO #Lanterns pic.twitter.com/R61q87Psp2

OMG the concept of having to wait another week pic.twitter.com/yOcGKss712 — stuff (@stuffiseeonline) August 24, 2026

OMG the concept of having to wait another week pic.twitter.com/yOcGKss712

Still, it's easy to see why fans might be excited for such a relatively small development. The last time we saw a live-action Hal Jordan wearing the mask was when Ryan Reynolds played the character for his 2011 standalone movie, and we all know how that went.

As the DCU comes together, moments like these can be just as important as the projects themselves. Fans clamored for a first look at Robert Pattinson as Batman and again flocked to see him throw on the cowl for The Batman Part 2 . David Corenswet's Superman drew eyes when his costume was revealed back in 2024 .

As Hal Jordan seemingly winds down his time as a Green Lantern, we've yet to see what Pierre's John Stewart looks like in the suit. We'll hopefully get a better look when he reprises his role for the DCU's Superman sequel, Man of Tomorrow , next year.

While we wait for Lanterns Episode 3 this weekend, August 30, you can see what IGN thought of Episode 2 . You can also learn about the villain some viewers think is hiding in plain sight , as well as what DC Studios co-CEO James Gunn had to say about the gritty tone for the new DCU series .

articles.title: These Huge One-Volume History Books Are on Sale for $0.99 Each
articles.summary: Two major one-volume history books published by Penguin are on sale for $0.99 each. The deal ends soon.
articles.body:
Heads up, amateur historians: here’s an incredible deal on two beefy tomes for your digital bookshelf. Penguin is running $0.99 sales on the Kindle ebook version of two of its biggest history books. The latest editions of The Penguin History of the World ( see at Amazon ) and The Penguin History of the United States of America ( see on Amazon ) are both on sale for $0.99 each . The sale ends tonight, so grab ‘em if you want to learn a thing or two for super cheap.

The Penguin History of the World: 6th Edition (Kindle Ebook)

The Penguin History of the World is currently in its 6th edition. It’s been a landmark book ever since J.M. Roberts published the first edition in 1976. Roberts was a renowned and popular British historian who updated the book many times over the ensuing decades until his death in 2003. At that point, Penguin brought on the wonderfully named historian Odd Arne Westad to continue editing and revising the tome. In physical form, it’s a doorstopper of a book, ringing in at 1,280 pages. If you grab this deal, the math works out to roughly $0.00077 per page.

The Penguin History of the United States of America: New Edition (Kindle Ebook)

As for The Penguin History of the USA, it was first published in 1985 as The Longman History of the United States of America. It’s by Hugh Brogan , a British historian and biographer who, it so happens, used to correspond regularly with J.R.R. Tolkien. In fact, a number of Tokien's letters to Brogan are included in The Letters of J.R.R. Tolkien ( see at Amazon ). Anyway, this book kicks off in 30,000 BCE, when it’s thought the first humans may have come over the land-bridge that’s now the Bering Strait, and runs up to the Reagan era of the 1980s.

If you’re like me and you’re not exactly a history buff , but you’re generally interested history as a concept, it can be hard to find good books to read. Most history books, after all, hone in on one time period, or one major historical event. That’s how historians (and most academics and professionals, for that matter) work: they specialize. But if you want a broad overview of all of human history? Or of the history of the United States? Decent one-volume books on those broad topics, that cover that much history, are a bit harder to find.

Penguin’s pair of history books are some of the most popular, and have been for decades. They go in chronological order, so you can follow the broad arc of history over centuries or millennia.

Again, the deals won’t last forever. There’s actually a ticking clock on the page for the USA history book; that deal ends at midnight Pacific Time. As for the History of the World, that one doesn’t have so definite an end, but you can bet it won’t be a buck forever, so add it to your Kindle library sooner than later if you’re interested.

articles.title: This Legend of Zelda Brain Teaser Recreates One of the Best Side Quests From Tears of the Kingdom
articles.body:
Tears of the Kingdom was an excellent game. IGN even went as far as to call it a perfect 10 out of 10 when it first came out on the Switch. And while the boss battles, gameplay, and massive open world definitely contributed to its masterpiece status, it was all of the little side quests that brought it all together for me.

One particular quest that made TotK's Ultrahand abilities shine was helping Addison put up President Hudson signs throughout Hyrule. Now, in 2026, that very quest has been brought into the real world with a brain teaser puzzle.

Legend of Zelda Addison Sign Hanayama Metal Brain Teaser

You have a lot less material to work with than many of the sign puzzles in the actual game, so you can't just start sticking massive boards to the bottom of the sign to keep it upright. Instead, you need to find a very specific solution.

Along with the sign (made of metal) and Addison himself, you have four metal logs to work with. The product page calls it "worthy of a level 6" challenge, so I wouldn't expect the solution to be straightforward.

Once you actually complete the brain teaser, you'll have a little metal figure of Addison and his President Hudson sign you can display on your desk or shelf. articles.title: France and Saudi Arabia to Build $7 Billion Dragon Ball Z Theme Park Outside Paris
articles.summary: France and Saudi Arabia have come to the mutual conclusion that the world needs Dragon Ball Z theme park. So, they’re building one near Paris to the tune of €6 billion ($7 billion USD).
articles.body:
France and Saudi Arabia have come to the mutual conclusion that the world needs Dragon Ball Z theme park. So, they’re building one near Paris to the tune of €6 billion ($7 billion USD).

The Elysee Palace announced the news on Monday, August 23, during the Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s visit to Paris. The idea was reportedly first sparked during the Crown Prince’s trip to the city last year, when he and French President Emmanuel Macron discovered their shared love for the iconic anime franchise.

The park will be constructed northwest of the capital city near Cergy-Pontoise, with the massive project expected to create approximately 22,000 jobs. Construction is predicted to take several years, with no opening date publicly announced as yet.

To no one’s surprise, Qiddiya is providing the funds for the project, which will be one of two Dragon Ball Z theme parks once all is said and done. The first theme park was officially revealed on the official Dragon Ball website back in 2024, along with extensive concept art and teasers for what it’ll look like when construction is complete.

The first park is currently being built in Qiddiya City, a massive entertainment hub currently in development just outside the capital of Riyadh. It will reportedly span more than 500,000 square meters, featuring seven recreations of locales from the series including the Kame House, Capsule Corporation, and Beerus's Planet.

Five rides will also be included as part of a 30+ attraction total, along with a 70-meter-tall statue of Shenron. It’s a massive undertaking, and one that isn’t expected to open anytime soon, with no official opening date released at the time of writing.

Dragon Ball Z Theme Park Concept Art (2024)

The announcement of Paris’s Dragon Ball theme park comes after the Esports World Cup was relocated to the city due to security concerns near Riyadh, where it was previously scheduled to take place. Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince was in attendance for the competition’s closing ceremony, where Macron was also present.

This is one of several expansive investments the country has made into cultural projects within the gaming and anime space; most recently, Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund completed a $55 billion acquisition of EA as part of an investor group alongside Silver Lake and Affinity Partners.

In March, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman's Electronic Gaming Development Company (EGDC) acquired a 5% stake in Capcom, upping its ownership in the famed Japanese game developer and publisher to 10%.

And back in February, Saudi-owned RTS took full ownership of Evo , the world’s largest fighting game tournament series, which has since expanded to include several other global Evo events in a controversial turn of events within the fighting game community.

articles.title: Canceled Iron Man Game Footage From Just Cause and Mad Max Developer Leaks Online
articles.summary: Alleged footage from Avalanche Studios' canceled Iron Man game has surfaced online.
articles.body:
Alleged footage from Avalanche Studios' canceled Iron Man game has surfaced online.

In the early 2010s, Just Cause and Mad Max developer Avalanche Studios was working on an Iron Man game . The project was never officially announced to the public, but Avalanche Studios co-founder Christofer Sundberg confirmed its development and cancellation during an interview in 2022. Now, gameplay for that title has popped up online via Reddit , reportedly sourced through a PS3 developer kit.

The gameplay is extremely unfinished, but it shows Iron Man flying around in a large environment, fighting jets and attacking various facilities. One of the more in-depth videos appears to be an unfinished E3 demo which shows Iron Man in hand-to-hand combat with soldiers, using a heavy, Arkham-esque style of combat. Of course, he also boasts his repulsors, missiles, and other gadgets to help take down all of his targets.

One of the more standout features is that the environments would've been at least semi-destructible. Iron Man can throw foes through walls, slice them apart in order to make shortcuts for himself, and tear up buildings around him. Beyond that, the build isn't far along enough to really distinguish itself much from SEGA's MCU Iron Man games. It certainly shows promise, though. Given how fun the studio's Mad Max game is and the sandbox gameplay of the Just Cause series, Avalanche probably would've made a killer Iron Man game.

There is still some hope, however. EA Motive is currently developing a new Iron Man game , though details on the project are extremely scarce. The project entered development in 2022, but there haven't been any updates since then. EA was also working on a Black Panther game, which was canceled last year . However, Iron Man has remained in development, despite fears that it will suffer the same fate. Given it has been four years since the announcement, hopefully we are close to hearing some news on the title.

articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Devs Vow to Update Captain Price After Botched Haircut Goes Viral
articles.summary: Publisher Activision and developer Infinity Ward have promised to update Captain Price's hair in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 after images of his botched haircut went viral.
articles.body:
Publisher Activision and developer Infinity Ward have promised to update Captain Price's hair in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 after images of his botched haircut went viral.

As last weekend's closed beta dredged up conversations revolving around its time-to-kill (TTK) speeds and problematic spawn placements, other fans aimed at Captain Price and his barber. It's mostly thanks to a few images that have circulated across social media, with fans pointing out that, maybe, Modern Warfare 4's version of the classic character should invest in some hair gel.

He looks…unwell, at least when compared to past versions of Captain Price. Whether he's chasing down Vladimir Makarov or walking you through a training course, Price is known to have a full head of hair and a beard that could make even Ghost blush. The one from Modern Warfare 4, however, has neither of those things, and according to many, he hardly looks like the Task Force 141 leader fans have come to know. Activision and Infinity Ward say that's not their intention, but there's also a good reason why only some Call of Duty fans are encountering this choppy imposter.

Still, the developers and Activision and Infinity Ward are going to do their best to give the Call of Duty fan-favorite Operator the head of hair he deserves. The studio community teams X/Twitter account replied to a few of the more popular posts, promising it would be addressed "in a future update."

"Captain Price's hair does not appear correctly when viewing his character model at the lowest level of detail," a tab in the "Known Issues" column from the Modern Warfare 4 Trello says.

Also noted in the Known Issues category are dropped framerates when cooking lethal weapons, hitches for PC players during their first multiplayer matches, a stuck loadout screen bug, and more. TTK is another issue the team is looking into , as are those spawns.

Beard Papa’s is teaming up with Persona to celebrate the RPG series’ 30th anniversary with some special cream puffs.

Beard Papa’s is a Japanese dessert chain with locations sprinkled across the US. It’s best known for its primary offering, cream puffs, which come in a variety of different flavors and combinations for customers to choose from.

Starting September 4, participating Beard Papa’s locations within the United States will transform their interiors and offer up several new flavors of cream puffs in collaboration with Persona.

Persona 4 Revival Release Date Trailer Xbox Games Showcase 2026 - Screenshots

These storefronts will feature Persona-themed digital menu boards, bakery case graphics, posters, television displays, and more, transforming them into a real-life Persona menu screen. And for mega-fans, the Beard Papa’s locations in Little Tokyo and Cerritos will include large-format anniversary murals specifically designed for photo opportunities.

Limited-time cream puff flavors are also on offer: Original Cream Puff, Matcha Cream Puff, Ube S'mores Cream Puff, Cookies & Cream Cream Puff, and the Double Berry Cream Puff, each inspired by specific games in the Persona series.

Four and six-pack gift sets are also available for purchase. The four-pack set comes with four featured cream puffs, a Persona chibi sticker sheet, and an in-game code card for Persona 5: The Phantom X. The six-pack set comes with six cream puffs, a blind-packed acrylic standee featuring one of eight designs, and an in-game code card for Persona 5: The Phantom X.

Of course, it wouldn’t be a collab if there wasn’t merchandise involved; you can also snag a ceramic mug, a T-shirt, zip hoodie, and eco tote bag as part of the Persona x Beard Papa’s partnership on the official Beard Papa’s website .

This collaboration lasts from September 4 to October 4, just in time to herald the next big developments for the Persona series. Persona 4 Revival, a full remake of Persona 4 Golden, is set to release in February 2027 , and Atlus is hard at work on the next entry in the franchise, Persona 6.

It’s a big time for Persona; a live-action adaptation is in the works at Netflix, with Christopher Monfette attached as writer, showrunner, and executive producer. 21 Laps' Shawn Levy and Robert Atwood are also attached to executive produce, alongside Sega’s Toru Nakahara.

Beyond that, Kazuhisa Wada, producer for Atlus' P-Studio, recently remarked that he believes the studio will “have to” do remakes of the first and second games in the Persona series, giving fans even more to look forward to as the days tick down to Persona 4 Revival’s release.

articles.title: Xbox and PlayStation Appear to Be Publicly Backing Down from Promoting Multiplatform Releases
articles.summary: Xbox and PlayStation seem to be downplaying their multiplatform presence in new marketing beats.
articles.body:
Xbox and PlayStation seem to be downplaying their multiplatform presence in new marketing beats.

As spotted by PushSquare , Xbox uploaded a new trailer for Minecraft Dungeons 2 on its YouTube channel, which doesn't make any mention of the game coming to PS5 or Nintendo Switch 2. However, the game's previous two trailers, released in March and June respectively, both clearly advertised every platform the title will be released on. It seems like Xbox may be pulling back even further on promoting its games for other platforms now under CEO Asha Sharma.

Earlier this summer, Xbox reportedly pulled the plug on a PS5 version of Gears of War: E-Day just ahead of its reveal. A piece of key art for the game was even shown on an Xbox podcast with a PS5 logo , which was later removed, indicating the decision may have been relatively last-minute. There were also reports that Microsoft pulled a trailer for Halo: Campaign Evolved from a PlayStation State of Play, a move by Sharma that reportedly created tensions between Xbox and PlayStation. It seems like Minecraft Dungeon 2's new trailer may be part of Xbox's strategy to bring players back into its own ecosystem and create brand strength.

Xbox isn't the only one changing its messaging, though. Earlier this year, it was reported that PlayStation is abandoning PC releases for its flashy first-party single-player games like Ghost of Yotei. The company had been releasing the majority of its first-party story-driven games on PC for about half a decade, but it doesn't appear to be part of the strategy going forward. As a result, PlayStation has embraced the "only on PlayStation" branding once again.

In a new PlayStation ad, the words "PlayStation 5 exclusive" are plastered across gameplay for Marvel's Wolverine, Ghost of Yotei, Astro Bot, Gran Turismo 7, Saros, and God of War Laufey. This is meant to signal to players that these games won't be making the jump to PC later and that the company is embracing full-blown exclusivity as it did for decades with the PS1, PS2, PS3, and some of the PS4 generation.

Xbox's strategy still seems a bit wishy-washy, on the other hand. The company has promised permanent exclusivity for Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution , but beyond that, it remains to be seen what will happen. Will The Elder Scrolls 6 be exclusive to Xbox? Will the Fallout 3 and New Vegas remasters be exclusive? Only time will tell.

articles.title: The Witcher 3 Songs of the Past Expansion Confirmed to Include More Gwent, and Everyone Is Already Celebrating
articles.summary: CD Projekt Red has confirmed The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt's upcoming Songs of the Past expansion will come with more Gwent, and card game lovers are already celebrating.
articles.body:
CD Projekt Red has confirmed The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt 's upcoming Songs of the Past expansion will come with more Gwent, and card game lovers are already celebrating.

The Witcher 3 earned a lot of praise when it launched back in 2015. While Doug Cockle 's gravelly delivery as Geralt helped sell its story, and its RPG gameplay quickly hooked in every kind of fantasy fan, many would say Gwent was what truly kept them coming back for more.

"In Gwent, gamers clash with friends in fast-paced duels that combine skill-based play with bluffing, and careful deck construction," an official description from CD Projekt Red says . "The game is played over a best-of-three series of rounds, as players unleash their hand by slinging spells and diverse units with special abilities, and use clever tricks to deceive their opponents."

CD Projekt Red's in-universe card game first launched within the third installment in its Witcher series before being transformed into a standalone spinoff in 2017 and a real-life tabletop experience in 2025. It's a formula others have unsuccessfully attempted to mimic, but few have managed to stand the test of time quite like Gwent. That's probably exactly why it will be making a comeback when the developer returns to The Witcher 3 with its Songs of the Past expansion in 2027.

CD Projekt Red community and social media manager Marcin Łukaszewski teased the return of the fan-favorite side activity when replying to a player on X/Twitter . When the fan said they hoped more Gwent would be included in the surprise expansion, Łukaszewski offered a simple reply: "Confirmed!"

It's been more than 10 years since The Witcher 3's last expansion, Blood and Wine, came out in 2016, and by the time Songs of the Past launches next year, that wait will have been even longer. CD Projekt Red has teased that this is a full-fledged add-on for the game's story, teasing earlier this year that it will serve as a prologue . In other words, don't expect it to be all Gwent all the time, but for those who have waited to sit down for another round of tabletop challenges, it sounds like there's already more than enough reason to be excited.

articles.title: Lenovo confirms Legion Go issues after gamers report bricked devices
articles.summary: ﻿I installed Lenovo’s forbidden BIOS and my Legion Go lived. You might be less lucky.
articles.body: When a company’s software update turns your computer into a useless brick, should fixes be free? Framework, the modular computer startup, apparently thinks so. But it’s not clear that computing giant Lenovo will go that far. Three weeks after a Redditor presented a nearly $300 repair bill for their handheld gaming PC — among other reports of damage and high repair bills — the company is breaking its silence. It says, in short: try holding down the power button longer, and if that fails, contact customer support. Here’s the statement Lenovo provided to The Verge, via communications director Jeff Witt: > Lenovo is aware that some Legion Go devices may experience a blank screen during installation of BIOS version V42. BIOS V42 was not distributed through Windows Update or Legion Space, and Lenovo has removed the update from its support website while we continue our validation work. Users who have successfully completed the V42 update should not need to take further action at this time. > If a device encounters a blank screen during V42 installation, users may try pressing and holding the power button for approximately 10 seconds, waiting approximately one minute, and then powering the device on again. If the device does not resume normal operation, customers should contact Lenovo Support for further assistance. > Lenovo continues to evaluate and validate future BIOS updates for Legion Go. On the official Lenovo forums, it appears another Lenovo employee may have weighed in, too: a “Daniel_Legion” claims the issue “should be repaired free of charge” if you’re under warranty. “In the case of out-of-warranty devices, it should be repaired free of charge, but please check local laws,” they write. [Image: The Lenovo forum topic where Daniel_Legion weighs in. But Daniel_Legion has no other visible posts on the Lenovo forums, and “we’ll repair it if local laws force us to” isn’t a particularly reassuring pitch, so we’re asking Lenovo to confirm his words and their meaning. Will Lenovo extend its warranty to cover bad BIOS bricks? It’s important to note that not every Legion Go was vulnerable to begin with. You’d need to have the original Legion Go 8APU1, not the Legion Go S or the Legion Go 2, and you would’ve had to download BIOS V42 (N3CN42WW) directly from the company’s website over the two or so months before Lenovo yanked it. Even then, you might have been safe. The other day, I chose violence and decided to install the forbidden BIOS V42 on my own Legion Go review unit, and… after a long, scary sequence of black screens and progress bars and warnings and more black screens that lasted six whole minutes, it booted up just fine. (Plays games, even lets me log into Windows by typing my PIN with the gamepad controls. I couldn’t do that right before the update.) [Image: BIOS V42 running fine on my Legion Go. Plays games and everything. Assuming Daniel_Legion is legit, it sounds like the investigation is still ongoing. A team in Europe was able to reproduce the issue with three out of three devices tested, but other teams weren’t able to see it at all, he told the Lenovo forums. “As such the issue is most likely related to specific component used on mainboards in certain batch or batches, or the issue needs to have specific circumstances to manifest,” he wrote. I strongly feel that a company shouldn’t need to fully investigate before reassuring customers. They should say “if we did it, we will fix it, even outside of warranty.” That’s what Framework did with its device-bricking BIOS update.

articles.title: Clutch Picks Up a Publisher as Maverick Games Partners with Focus Entertainment
articles.summary: Focus Entertainment has announced it has forged a “major publishing partnership” with independent racing studio Maverick Games for its upcoming project, Clutch, after Amazon backed out earlier this year.
articles.body:
Focus Entertainment has announced it has forged a “major publishing partnership” with independent racing studio Maverick Games for its upcoming project, Clutch. The company notes the deal “strengthens Focus Entertainment’s portfolio with its first entry into the open-world racing space.”

“At Focus, we look to partner with creators who are redefining their genre,” said Focus deputy CEO Vincent Chataignier in a statement published in conjunction with the announcement. “Mike Brown and his team are regarded as one of the defining creative voices in the racing genre, and Clutch embodies exactly the creative ambition Focus Entertainment wants to champion.”

Clutch is set to arrive on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC early- to mid-2027.

If you missed IGN’s previous coverage of Clutch , it’s a rather glorious-looking racing and driving game that merges circuit racing, street racing, and wild, Fast & Furious-style action and heists. Set in an open-world world inspired by the iconic Mediterranean coastline of the French Riviera, Clutch will feature a map that encompasses Monaco, Cannes, and Saint-Tropez. With a heavy focus on customisation, Clutch will also boast a wild assortment of crazy car-based gadgets to use during its action-based missions, including a grappling hook that can slingshot your car around tight corners.

Founded in 2022 and spearheaded by a number of veterans of Forza Horizon developer Playground Games, Maverick Games had initially partnered with Amazon to publish Clutch . However, Amazon backed out of publishing the project earlier this year , citing the decision was part of a “strategic evolution.”

articles.title: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil Movie Includes First-Person Sequences — and Yes, Umbrella Is Involved
articles.summary: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie will pay homage to the series' first-person gameplay, newly-released footage has revealed.
articles.body:
Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie will pay homage to the series' first-person gameplay, newly-released footage has revealed.

A fresh video featuring Cregger discussing his upcoming horror adaptation also includes several quick shots from a first-person perspective, with the barrel of a shotgun and pistol raised directly in front of the camera.

The first moment sees a character — presumably Austin abrams' protagonist Bryan — sneaking through a house with a double-barrelled shotgun raised. The next shot we see is from behind the hands of a character — presumably Bryan again — holding a pistol as a zombie woman leaps towards him, and the camera.

𝙵𝚘𝚛 𝚝𝚑𝚎 𝚕𝚘𝚟𝚎 𝚘𝚏 𝚝𝚑𝚎 𝚐𝚊𝚖𝚎. From the mind of Zach Cregger, director of Weapons and Barbarian. Filmed for IMAX – Resident Evil is in theatres 9.18. #ResidentEvilㅤ pic.twitter.com/BHnhoinFS3 — Resident Evil (@ResidentEvil) August 24, 2026

𝙵𝚘𝚛 𝚝𝚑𝚎 𝚕𝚘𝚟𝚎 𝚘𝚏 𝚝𝚑𝚎 𝚐𝚊𝚖𝚎. From the mind of Zach Cregger, director of Weapons and Barbarian. Filmed for IMAX – Resident Evil is in theatres 9.18. #ResidentEvilㅤ pic.twitter.com/BHnhoinFS3

In his commentary, Cregger discusses how his movie will pay homage to how the Resident Evil games typically start players off with a simple pistol, before granting access to a shotgun and later a machine gun. We can see this in the footage shown so far, with the zombie woman seemingly the first undead that Bryan encounters (he hits her on the road) before he takes shelter in a nearby house (and finds a shotgun inside).

And if you're sat there confused as to why first-person is now a thing in Resident Evil, well, the series has evolved a long way since the fixed-camera perspectives of the original Resident Evil 1. Several recent entries have featured a first-person viewpoint, which is also optional in this year's Resident Evil Requiem.

Another behind-the-scenes movie detail has also been released: a document showing the delivery note for Bryan's medical cargo. This is, deliberately, exactly the kind of collectible players find in Resident Evil games, offering a little more detail on what's going on. And indeed, here we see that Bryan's courier charges are being billed to... "Umbrella Corp."

𝚈𝚘𝚞 𝚏𝚘𝚞𝚗𝚍 𝙱𝚛𝚢𝚊𝚗’𝚜 𝚍𝚎𝚕𝚒𝚟𝚎𝚛𝚢 𝚍𝚎𝚝𝚊𝚒𝚕𝚜. From the mind of Zach Cregger, director of Weapons and Barbarian. Filmed for IMAX – Resident Evil is in theatres 9.18. #ResidentEvilㅤ pic.twitter.com/Nv0r96SBzG — Resident Evil (@ResidentEvil) August 24, 2026

𝚈𝚘𝚞 𝚏𝚘𝚞𝚗𝚍 𝙱𝚛𝚢𝚊𝚗’𝚜 𝚍𝚎𝚕𝚒𝚟𝚎𝚛𝚢 𝚍𝚎𝚝𝚊𝚒𝚕𝚜. From the mind of Zach Cregger, director of Weapons and Barbarian. Filmed for IMAX – Resident Evil is in theatres 9.18. #ResidentEvilㅤ pic.twitter.com/Nv0r96SBzG

Umbrella was always going to be a part of this movie, as it is set in Raccoon City concurrently with its big zombie outbreak. But how much the company will actually be involved remains to be seen. Cregger has repeatedly made clear that this film will not cross paths with known characters or re-tell story that's already present in Capcom's games.

Indeed, eagle-eyed fans have known for a while this is something of an alternate universe take on Raccoon City's zombie outbreak — which now happens in snow-covered streets and is set in the modern day, meaning characters use smartphones. (Canonically, the city's zombie outbreak happens within the Resident Evil games in September 1998.)

Has Cregger found the right balance between an original story that also pays homage to the source material for existing Resident Evil fans? There's not long left to wait until we find out. Resident Evil arrives in theaters on September 18. Last month, Cregger revealed how the filming of one particular sequence almost killed Austin Abrams when a stunt went slightly wrong .

articles.title: GTA 6 Leak Subpoena: Discord Says It Will 'Evaluate the Validity and Scope Before Responding'
articles.summary: Discord has countered online reports about Take-Two’s hunt for the identity of the GTA 6 leaker, saying it has yet to be formally served a subpoena, and when it does receive it, it will take a long, hard look at it before responding.
articles.body:
Discord has countered online reports about Take-Two’s hunt for the identity of the GTA 6 leaker, saying it has yet to be formally served a subpoena, and when it does receive it, it will take a long, hard look at it before responding.

On Friday, Andrew L. Carter Jr., Judge of the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, granted Take-Two's request to subpoena Discord to divulge identifying information about users the Rockstar owner believes are tied to the leaks.

Take-Two’s subpoena of Microsoft was also granted. But while Microsoft has issued a statement to say it’s happy to work with Take-Two and Rockstar to help unearth the GTA 6 leaker, Discord issued a different line overnight.

Every Detail in the GTA 6 Cover Art Explained

“I can share an update on this,” Discord marketing director Ryan K. Rigney said in a tweet . “Discord has not yet been served with a subpoena from Take-Two. When we do, we'll evaluate the validity and scope before responding.”

Take-Two issued the subpoenas alleging Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) infringement. It wants information and records relating to the ‘CyberLeek’ account, which is allegedly behind the GTA 6 leaks. The subpoenas request identifying information associated with user accounts that were members of a number of Discord servers. One of the Discord servers mentioned in the filing is 'discord.gg/darkviperau,' which is described as the DarkViperAU editors' server. DarkViperAU is the online name of Australian GTA content creator Matthew "Matt" Judge, who has 2.27 million subscribers on YouTube and nearly 900,000 followers on Twitch. Judge has denied any wrongdoing .

Reclaim The Net, a group that advocates for free speech and privacy, criticised the Discord subpoena in a tweet.

“Copyright law is supposed to target infringement,” it said. “Here, it’s being used to hunt for identities. Take-Two is seeking DMCA subpoenas that could expose users who didn’t leak or upload GTA VI footage, but who participated in conversations within Discord servers where the leak was discussed."

In an article, Reclaim The Net continued : "One of the Discord servers in question has over 107,000 members, and while it is not clear if Take-Two is going after each and every one of them, the request does say 'all identifying information associated with all user accounts' that were or are members of three named servers since June 1 – and that participated in a conversation in those servers.

"In this case, Take-Two Interactive's one filings make it clear that they're not limited to whoever is uploading the leaks, they're targeting entire communities and channels that are merely existing in the same Discord server as those alleged leakers.

"This is now the pursuit of a membership list under the color of the enforcement of copyright. While it can be crushed if people push back, there's actually nothing about the DMCA process that discourages this in a strong enough way.

"To file a claim is cheap and quick, and the compliance cost falls on the platforms. There was a time when companies would at least try to maintain the guise that their targets were limited to infringement but, these days, they're getting more brazen and now hitting anyone who happens to have been standing nearby."

It is unclear if Microsoft has actually been served with Take-Two’s subpoena, either, although according to court documents it looks like Microsoft had already launched an investigation of its own into the CyberLeek account. Meanwhile, the subpoena for Twitter / X has yet to be signed off, but that may simply be a formality.

All the while, the GTA 6 leaks continue , and there is fresh concern that CyberLeek will release significant story spoilers. Neither Rockstar nor Take-Two have issued a statement. IGN has asked for comment.

GTA 6 is due out on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S on November 19, 2026.

articles.title: [UPDATE] GTA 6 Leaker Releases Game Store, Nightclub and Beach Gameplay Videos, Defends Crypto Scheme
articles.summary: The GTA 6 leaks have continued, this time with two new gameplay videos and a message from the leaker defending their crypto scheme.
articles.body:
UPDATE: CyberLeek has dropped a third GTA 6 leak video today following on fast from this morning's early releases featuring a nightclub and a beach scene — marking a significant escalation in the amount of footage hitting the internet.

This latest release of leaked material also continues to push CyberLeek's supposed agenda behind the leaks: an apparent dislike of the fact that physical media is being abandoned. "People are confused," reads the latest message watermarked into the footage. "This is not about actual discs. It is about ownership. Resale rights still matter — even in a digital-only era."

Fittingly, this message is overlaid on gameplay that shows GTA 6 protagonist Jason exploring a video game store, complete with spoof consoles (that look a lot like PS5) and game cases (I wonder if they include the discs!) There's even a sign in the store advertising "ex-rental games and movies for sale." Titles on offer in the fictional shop include games such as Glory Souls 2, Desolate Rim, We Came Together.

The leaks certainly appear to be ramping up ahead of Netflix's official GTA 6 reveal ( check out the global release times here ).

UPDATE: Hot on the heels of the nightclub gameplay leak, CyberLeek has released a 13th video, this time showing off Jason cycling on a beach packed with NPCs.

This new video includes the same watermarked memecoin advertisement and crypto statement detailed in the original story, below.

ORIGINAL STORY: The GTA 6 leaks have continued, this time with a new gameplay video and a message from the leaker defending their crypto scheme.

This 12th video leak shows relatively unremarkable nightclub gameplay, and includes the now standard advertisement of the 'CyberLeek' token at the heart of the cryptocurrency scheme that is believed to be the motivating factor behind all this.

But this new video also includes a watermarked message that defends the crypto scheme. “Stop the hate,” the message reads. “Channel that energy into protests. Not at those actually fighting for you. CL is taking huge risks in this battle. Leeks are free and donations cover operational costs. Using crypto is the only way. CL can’t win alone. Today is the day to show support and protest.”

Every Detail in the GTA 6 Cover Art Explained

CyberLeek has launched paid-for polls with a number of gameplay video choices people can vote on by sending tokens. People have spent hundreds of dollars' worth of the tokens to vote . This crypto scheme is ostensibly about protesting our all-digital future and Rockstar’s decision not to sell GTA 6 on-disc. At least one person showed up at Rockstar North in Scotland, filming themselves eating a leek outside the office.

There is growing concern that CyberLeek will release damaging story spoilers, with one poll option a prologue featuring Lucia. So far, the leaked gameplay videos have shown dual protagonist Jason only.

CyberLeek has continued to release GTA 6 gameplay videos for eight days straight despite Take-Two's subpoenas of Microsoft, Discord, and X / Twitter as part of the company's hunt for identifying information. We are now just two days away from Netflix’s timed-exclusive GTA 6 reveal, which is set to show gameplay officially for the first time.

From a Take-Two and Rockstar perspective, significant damage is being done. According to Bloomberg , Rockstar still doesn’t know how these leaks happened, nor who is behind them. And while there are no plans to shift this week’s big Netflix reveal, Bloomberg reported that there is frustration and anger internally at recent events, with management sending morale-boosting emails to staff.

Former Rockstar Games technical director Obbe Vermeij, however, downplayed the damage caused by the leaks . Vermeij, who worked at Rockstar North from 1995 to 2009, took to social media to say the Hot Coffee scandal was much more damaging than these GTA 6 leaks.

Neither Take-Two nor Rockstar has issued a statement on the GTA 6 leaks. IGN has asked for comment.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: Jason David Frank's Final Movie, Legend of the White Dragon, Won’t Be as Memorable as He Was
articles.summary: Legend of the White Dragon review: Jason David Frank's final movie won’t be as memorable as he was.
articles.body:
Legend of the White Dragon will be released in theaters on August 28.

Let’s get one thing straight up front: Legend of the White Dragon is not a Power Rangers movie.

Yes, for those of my generation that grew up watching Power Rangers, it does include plenty of familiar faces, putting the late Jason David Frank (Mighty Morphin Power Rangers) as well as Jason Faunt (Time Force) and Ciara Hanna (Megaforce) front and center in what is a clear nostalgia play to draw in fans of the original shows. There are even moments in the movie where, if you really squint hard enough, it can almost look and feel like a more adult version of a Power Rangers show… not in the way that the largely forgotten 2017 movie did, but in how the visual effects are often quite shaky and there’s a big ol’ heaping of earnest cheesiness poured over it. It all makes this Kickstarter-funded project play more like a YouTube fan film than a standalone work, but there can be a charm to such an endeavor, and there is something admirable in the abstract about a group of people coming together to make a movie like this.

Unfortunately, while there remains plenty of actual charm in the shows this movie’s cast became known for, that’s utterly lacking in the execution here as the entire thing comes apart with shocking speed. Even as it was able to create its own thing, Legend of the White Dragon feels like a sequel weighed down by a whole series of movies that nobody in the audience has actually seen. There are flashbacks on top of flashbacks, pages of stilted dialogue in one belabored exposition scene after another, and woefully stiff fight sequences that never leave much of a mark. While a movie like this doesn’t need to be as thrilling and kinetic as the recent action stunner, The Furious , it’s still tough going when it can’t actually land a believable punch. More closely resembling the works of Neil Breen — the ultra-low-budget filmmaker known for Double Down, Fateful Findings, and Twisted Pair — but with some more money to throw at things, it’s occasionally unintentionally funny, though mostly a drag.

Our hero-turned-pariah is Erik Reed (Frank); he is believed by many to be, if not in hiding, dead following what characters refer to as "Dark Day," which is essentially a battle he took part in that killed 1,263 innocent people. Don’t worry about remembering any of this: Everything, including this exact number, will get repeated over and over as the movie spends far too long arranging and rearranging deck chairs before it feels like it’s actually even properly starting. Though we’re informed Erik was more of a treasure hunter than a superhero — leading to the hilarious line, “he left behind his most precious treasures, his wife and child” — he’ll soon have to step up and become one when he gets hunted down by those looking to take him in or get revenge. It’s all shallow and broad with a simulacrum of a complex and engaging central superhero character. Sure, he has abilities that come from a crystal which make him so powerful that he can fly into the sky, but while the story builds to him being unleashed to do so, the actual movie surrounding him doesn’t come remotely close to taking flight.

It’s at the secluded boxing ring where Erik has been hiding, which comes complete with old newspaper clippings taped on the wall that outline what we’ve already been told has happened, where we get our first fight. What could have been a goofy brawl, with fighters leaping through the air like wrestlers and smashing concrete blocks on heads, doesn’t actually cut loose. For one thing, the smashing of the concrete block comes down on a motorcycle helmet clearly meant to hide a stunt performer, leaving no sense of actual impact. Even more disappointing, the shaky camera work further obscures the stunts rather than letting us see the choreography clearly. Fight sequences not only can but should be a dance, with camera and performer working together; in Legend of the White Dragon, each proves to have two left feet, never once feeling in sync with the other as it all just shuffles along.

The longer this drags on, the more this ostensibly stand-alone movie just feels like it was conceived to bring together the cast without any thought about what that would actually look like. Once the first already clunky action scene comes to a close, there are large stretches where the film just spins its wheels, leaning heavily on the recurring presence of King Bach as a hologram to explain what’s going on. This may sound on paper like it could be a bit silly or even fun, but there’s no playfulness here. No matter how much the cast is all game, the atrocious dialogue and general lack of movement makes it a scattered slog. Even with brief moments where the actors bounce off each other in some more potentially fun ways, it always falls back to flashbacks which bring everything to a screeching halt, or bits with a one-note villain who can’t create a truly menacing presence.

When the final big confrontation and forced tease for a sequel arrives, you’re left wondering how a movie less than 90 minutes long can feel like it’s pushing two hours. Fans of the cast might still just be glad to spend time with their favorite actors, but both they and the performers deserve better than the slapped-together final film we get here. Despite all the legacies it's gesturing toward and the memorable ensemble it showcases, Legend of the White Dragon is nothing more than a forgettable misfire and miles away from legendary.

articles.title: The TCL Note A1 is a kinder, gentler tablet
articles.summary: It’s easy on the eyes, comes with a stylus, and got me to write out an 1,100 word review by hand. But it isn’t E-Ink.
articles.body: Without thinking, I scribbled over what I’d just written.  It’s what I would have done if I was writing with pen and paper. But I didn’t have a pen in my hand; my canvas was an LCD and the letters on my page were just pixels. Score one point to the TCL Note A1. TCL’s Note A1 Nxtpaper tablet (its full government name) is supposed to make you forget that you’re using a tablet. It has one of the company’s signature low-glare matte displays and ships with a stylus. The pen’s haptics even mimic the scratching of a pencil on paper. On the software side, the A1 takes a lot of cues from the Remarkable tablet. Instead of a typical Android home screen, you get a page with shortcuts to recent notes and a snapshot of the day’s calendar events. You can download any app you want from the Google Play Store, but that would spoil what I think is the A1’s nicest feature: the ability to trick you into forgetting that you’re using a gadget at all. [Product: TCL Note A1 Nxtpaper | The Note A1 occupies the space between a full-fledged tablet and a low-distraction E-Ink device like the Remarkable Pro. It has a full color LCD screen with a 120Hz refresh rate. You can watch videos and scroll a website as you normally would — something that just doesn’t work on E-Ink tablets. But the A1 is a note-taking device first and foremost, shipping with a pressure-sensitive stylus with adjustable haptics to mimic the scratchy feeling of writing on paper. It’s not like, “I can’t believe it’s not real paper” levels of convincing, but it’s good enough that you can lose yourself in the act of writing. I did, at least, enough to forget about the “eraser” on the other end of the stylus. Unfortunately, the Note A1 falls into the classic trap of trying to offer the best of both worlds: it ends up feeling like it’s not quite here nor there. As a tablet, it’s just okay. Its 8GB of RAM are enough to help it chew through a media-dense web page with a little juddering. The LCD is honestly nicer than I expected, with generous viewing angles and vivid colors. But its blacks aren’t as rich as an OLED’s, and a little dimming in one corner of my review unit gives it away. The built-in speakers are fine in a pinch but sound tinny, and there are no physical volume buttons, which is a bizarre thing to omit. [Image: The stylus attaches magnetically to the side of the tablet, where it also charges. As an e-reader and note-taking device, it does the job but lacks the precision of a purpose-built device like the Remarkable. The home screen looks like a generic notes app’s main screen, plus a collapsible side panel where you can access other apps and system settings. I love a minimalist home screen as much as the next overstimulated millennial, but I wish it was more customizable. You can hide the two widgets at the top of the screen, including the “Inspiration Space” (more on that later) and change how your assortment of note collections appear, but you can’t do much more than that. Neither can you create your own cover design for your note collections — you’re stuck with some bland options that have TCL branding on them. TCL’s Max Ink Mode also would have been a nice addition here. The company’s other Nxtpaper tablets and phones offer this monochrome mode to simulate more of an e-reader experience and extend battery life by a lot. I’m surprised it’s missing.   I also had trouble while writing out a note and kept accidentally triggering the “back” navigation gesture at the side of the screen while writing this review. (Spoiler alert: I wrote my whole first draft on the tablet itself. Please applaud.) TCL doesn’t offer a way to disable this while writing, and though the notes app always saved my work before exiting, it was jarring. Still, the A1 has some standout strengths. It comes with a massive 8,000mAh battery and will easily hold up to a couple of days of continuous use. There’s a toggle in quick settings to turn on an eye comfort mode to cut down on blue light, and you can adjust the color temperature warmth to your liking. The stylus’ pressure sensitivity feels restrained yet responsive. I had the best time with the A1 when I forgot all about its tablet-ness and just embraced it as a canvas for doodles and writings. The A1 has a suite of AI features that all sound pretty familiar by now. With a dedicated button on the stylus you can highlight text and images to add to the “Inspiration Space,” a repository for things you might otherwise keep in a thousand idle Chrome tabs. You can group these clippings, along with your notes and doodles, into collections. Reminiscent of Pixel Screenshots, it uses AI to analyze and tag the items you add so you can cross-reference them and find it all later. I gave it an honest try and used it to organize some information and #inspo for my endless yard project. I recorded audio of a call with our landscape designer, running the transcript on one side of the screen and hand-writing notes on the other. This is exactly the kind of scenario tech companies love to pitch for devices like this, and yeah, it was neat. The voice transcription was very good, and an AI-generated summary of the call caught all the main takeaways. I had a harder time getting useful analysis from the AI in the Inspiration Space. I put the call transcript and all my related doodles and screenshots into a folder, thinking I’d be able to tap the ever-present “Ask AI” chip for some high-level analysis. It failed to identify the images I’d added and played dumb when I asked it questions it could have found answers to in the transcript. Bummer. [Image: This keyboard case is unfortunately not sold in the US right now. Aside from my disappointment with AI features — not for the first or last time! — I had a good time with the Note A1. I wish it came with Max Ink Mode. It’s not your best choice for a tablet-first, note-taking-second device. There’s an iPad for that. And Remarkable offers a better writing and note-keeping experience for purists. But if you’re after a decent digital writing experience and still want tablet features on the side, the A1 does the job. Certainly for a lot less money than an iPad Air or Pro with an Apple Pencil Pro — that combo will start just under $900 and only goes up from there. I think the best endorsement I can give of the Note A1 is that I enjoyed it enough to write out my entire review on it by hand. I think it will also be the last blog I write out by hand, but it was pretty satisfying. You just don’t get the same effect with a Google Doc. Photography by Allison Johnson / The Verge

articles.title: 'Appalling and Fundamentally Dishonest': Mark Ruffalo Slams Paramount After Studio Suggests Warner Bros. Buyout Criticism Stemmed From 'Antisemitic Tropes'
articles.summary: Avengers star Mark Ruffalo has responded to the suggestion he invoked "antisemitic tropes" in his ongoing criticism of Paramount's $111 billion Warner Bros. buyout.
articles.body:
Avengers star Mark Ruffalo has responded to the suggestion he had invoked "antisemitic tropes" in his ongoing criticism of Paramount's $111 billion Warner Bros. buyout.

Responding to the claim, made in a lengthy and unusual statement by Paramount itself, Ruffalo dubbed the accusation as "appalling and fundamentally dishonest."

The issue stems from Ruffalo's continued pressure on Paramount over its controversial takeover of Warner Bros. , a transaction that Ruffalo and numerous other Hollywood stars have said will likely result in consolidation, cost-cutting and job losses, plus particular concern surrounding the independence of Warner Bros.' news organization CNN. Paramount is owned by David Ellison, and the buyout's finances will be backed his father Larry Ellison, the billionaire co-founder of technology firm Oracle and the world's sixth-richest person.

In an Instagram story last week, Ruffalo commented on a video featuring Oracle vice chair Safra Catz, who discussed Oracle's public backing of the Israeli military in the wake of October 7 terrorist attacks, and the subsequent deployment of what she described as Oracle's "really profoundly scary technology" to the Israeli army.

"These 'really profoundly scary technologies' will most likely be merged into one of the largest media conglomerates in the world and one day used on you," Ruffalo wrote in response. "Look how she revels in what we now have come to see as a genocide, which was built on an apartheid system of oppression powered by Oracle.

"We have a chance to stop this," the actor continued. "There are 12 state Attorneys General suing to block this merger. It will be catastrophic for our film industry. Mergers like this one are almost always bad for workers, consumers and the industry they tend to dominate. It's a classic antitrust case. It will hike up the cost of cable and flatten out competition. This means less choice for our audiences. It also concentrates an enormous amount of creative control to companies that say and do things like this strange woman from Oracle."

In a response statement issued to The Hollywood Reporter , a Paramount spokesperson took the unusual step of directly quoting and discussing Ruffalo's Instagram story, branding his message as containing "antisemitic tropes" and suggesting that such statements expose "the true motivation of some who have advocated opposition to this transaction." Paramount's response lies below in full:

"We are, as always, troubled when antisemitic tropes are invoked in purported service of a business dispute," the Paramount spokesperson stated. "Words like 'genocide' and 'apartheid,' applied to a corporate transaction, aren't just wrong — they're a bridge too far, and they cheapen the very real suffering those words are meant to describe. This doesn't deserve a response in kind — and to be clear, we don't tolerate prejudice of any kind, against anyone.

"This brings us to a moment to lower the temperature, not raise it. We'd rather build than further engage in such rhetoric. This simply exposes the true motivation of some who have advocated opposition to this transaction. On the other hand, our commitment to great content is matched by our commitment to acceptance – to every story, every storyteller, and no blacklists, no exceptions, for anyone.

"We understand people feel strongly about this merger and are hopeful and expect that it will be judged based on the legal merits, not underlying bias. We're asking for the same good faith we're extending: less rhetoric, more understanding. Paramount's future is being written for everyone who wants to make and watch great stories."

It's this statement from Paramount that Ruffalo has now responded again to condemn, in a post on X/Twitter which seeks to separate his criticism of Oracle and its links with the Israeli military from the suggestion that such criticism cannot exist without being antisemitic. Ruffalo's response lies below in full:

"The accusation that I am antisemitic is appalling and fundamentally dishonest. Criticizing the actions of the Israeli prime minister, a military technology contract, or the executives who supply it is not the same as criticizing Jewish people. This critical and necessary dialogue is then dishonestly framed as being anti-Israel. To be clear, my views come from my own political convictions and should never be interpreted as hostility toward Jewish people, for whom I have deep love and respect. Everything I know about acting, activism, and humanism has been profoundly shaped by the Jewish friends, colleagues, and loved ones who have been integral and family throughout every point of my life.

"This merger has real consequences for real people, and for the entire country. Scrutinizing the Ellisons, including Oracle’s business built on data, surveillance technology and government contracts, and the serious threat to editorial freedom and the loss of a livelihood for thousands of families, is fair and necessary. The $111 billion deal would hand one family control over CNN, HBO and Warner Bros., backed in part by foreign money whose influence on editorial decisions has never been fully explained to the public.

"Lawmakers on both sides of the aisle have called for serious national security review, and regulators still haven't given the public a real answer. Until they do, the merger shouldn’t move forward. Now is the time to dive boldly into all these issues, not step back or concede."

Last month, Paramount's buyout of Warner Bros. was postponed until the conclusion of an antitrust trial , which could keep the deal from closing until the legal process is concluded, or June 2027 at the latest. Ruffalo, meanwhile, was most recently seen in portraying his veteran Marvel character Bruce Banner/The Hulk in Spider-Man: Brand New Day , which has now passed $2.22 million at the box office.

articles.title: The OLED Xbox Ally X20 officially starts at $1,300
articles.summary: You can pre-order a standalone Xbox Ally X20 handheld with OLED screen at Best Buy or Asus’s online store for $1,300, shipping October 15th.
articles.body: The Asus Xbox Ally X20 looked like it could be one of the best handheld gaming PCs yet made — but originally, Asus wanted you to buy a bundle pairing it with pricy AR glasses. In July, we told you that bundle would no longer be necessary, and today it’s official: you can pre-order a standalone handheld at Best Buy or Asus’s online store for $1,300, shipping October 15th. Asus spokesperson Don Nguyen tells us it’s the same basic ROG 20th Anniversary handheld I tried at its US offices, so you should be getting a translucent gadget with gold trim. Bling isn’t the reason to buy it, though. If I were buying, it’d be because of the larger new 7.4-inch 1080p OLED screen, the clearest, fastest, and brightest on a handheld yet. I’d be buying for the extra-comfy grips, the trick D-pad that rotates between 4-way and 8-way, and the lack of an Xbox “Library” button to yank me out of my game. You can read my full preview here, though I always recommend waiting for the reviews — my review of the rival MSI Claw EX found issues that were invisible in my preview, after all. Personally, I think $1,300 is an awful lot to spend on a handheld, but I’m pleased that it “only” costs $300 more than the original $1,000 Xbox Ally X, especially since that $1,000 model and the $600 Xbox Ally will continue to stick around, Asus rep Anthony Spence confirms. But if you have $2,500 to spend, Asus is making the bundled version a bit more attractive. Not only will it include the $1,300 Xbox Ally X20 and a matching pair of 240Hz ROG XREAL X1 glasses (normally $849), it’ll also come with a matching Dbrand Killswitch protective case for the handheld (with the hardshell screen cover, stick toppers and built-in kickstand), plus a branded Pelican case to carry everything in. Here’s the bundle: [Image: And here’s another photo of the Dbrand Killswitch around the handheld: [Image: The Xbox Ally X20 won’t be the most powerful handheld (that’ll currently be a Strix Halo device like the upcoming $1,750 GPD Win Max 3) or even the most powerful handheld that feels properly portable (that’ll be the Claw EX), and it certainly won’t be the most affordable. But it might be the most refined and comfortable to use among Windows handhelds. We’ll find out this fall.
